__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source scraping the assistant server.

title: NetBird AI Assistant

panels.title: Service up
panels.description: 0 = Prometheus cannot scrape an instance. The first thing to check.

panels.title: Chats today
panels.description: Distinct conversations since midnight UTC. The product's usage number.

panels.title: Active users today
panels.description: Distinct users who sent a turn today.

panels.title: Turn error ratio
panels.description: Share of chat turns that failed. Closer to what a user feels than the HTTP 5xx rate, which misses a turn that 200s and then breaks mid-stream.

panels.title: Turn latency p95
panels.description: Whole turn — doc-tool loop and suggestions included, not just the first model call.

panels.title: Cost per chat (p50)
panels.description: What a typical chat costs today. Estimated from tokens — see telemetry/pricing.ts.

panels.title: Spend today
panels.description: Estimated spend across all chats since midnight UTC.

panels.title: Prompt cache hit ratio
panels.description: Prompt tokens served from cache. With a system prompt this size it is the biggest single lever on cost — a sustained drop usually means the prompt prefix changed.

panels.title: Turn outcomes
panels.description: answer = the model answered; tool_use = handed off to the caller; question = asked the user; error = the turn failed.

panels.title: Turn duration p50 / p95
panels.description: The whole streamed turn — doc-tool loop and suggestions included — unlike HTTP latency, which ends when the stream opens.

panels.title: Worst tool + reason pairs (selected range)

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (tool, reason) (increase(netbird_assistant_tool_failures_total{env=~"$env", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))

panels.description: The work queue. A reason climbing on one tool is usually a schema or executor bug, not the model being careless. The matching sample is in the logs: event=tool_failure.

panels.title: Failed steps by reason
panels.description: unknown climbing means the classifier in telemetry/signals.ts needs a new pattern — treat it as a signal about that file, not noise.

panels.title: User sentiment
panels.description: How users talk to the assistant when it is going wrong. frustration is the one to watch — it is a bug report nobody files. Counts only; the text is never stored.

panels.title: Stop reasons
panels.description: max_tokens here means users got truncated answers — the most user-visible failure that never shows up as an error.

panels.title: Guardrail pre-screen verdicts
panels.description: Only runs when GUARDRAIL_INPUT_CLASSIFIER=true. error = the classifier failed and the request was allowed through.

panels.title: PII values redacted by kind
panels.description: Server-side backstop replacing identifiers before the model sees them. Non-zero means the frontend's pseudonymizer let something through.

panels.title: Cost per chat over time
panels.description: mean vs p50 vs p95 per chat. Divergence is the signal: it means one kind of conversation is carrying the bill.

panels.title: Token throughput by type
panels.description: cache_read dwarfing input is the healthy shape. input overtaking it means the cached prefix is being missed and cost is climbing.

panels.title: Cost per chat (p95)
panels.description: The expensive tail — long tool-driven builds, not one-line questions.

panels.title: Unpriced model calls
panels.description: Calls whose model has no entry in pricing.ts. Above zero means every cost number here reads low — add the model family to that table.

panels.title: Model calls today by task
panels.description: chat vs guardrail vs suggestions. The auxiliary tasks are cheap per call but run on every turn.

panels.title: Model call rate by model & status
LLM errors by code
panels.description: rate_limit/overloaded are the provider pushing back; auth means this deployment is misconfigured.

panels.title: Model calls per turn
panels.description: Above 1 means the server looped on doc tools before answering. A rising p95 is latency the user feels.

panels.title: Server tool outcomes
panels.description: blocked = refused by a precondition, not a failure. Rising error is a server-run tool (docs, API) breaking.

panels.title: Server tool latency p95 by tool
Doc cache hit ratio
panels.description: Shared public docs/API cache. A low ratio means repeated fetches of the same page — latency inside the turn.

panels.title: Mutating vs read-only tool calls
panels.description: How much of what the assistant proposes would change the account. A jump in mutating is worth understanding.

panels.title: Tokens today
panels.description: Input + output since midnight UTC — the quantity the usage limits count. Survives restarts (read from llm_usage).

panels.title: Active users this month
panels.description: Distinct users this calendar month (UTC).

panels.title: HTTP latency (/v1/chat)

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(netbird_assistant_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=~"$env", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", route="/v1/chat"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(netbird_assistant_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=~"$env", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", route="/v1/chat"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(netbird_assistant_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=~"$env", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", route="/v1/chat"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.description: Handler latency, not stream lifetime — a long SSE stream is not counted here. Use turn duration for what the user waits.

panels.title: Rejections by reason
panels.description: Why requests were refused, which the status code cannot say. usage_limit means customers are hitting their token ceiling; rate_limited means burst.

panels.title: Telemetry queue depth
panels.description: Rows buffered before the batched insert. Sustained growth means Postgres is not keeping up.

panels.title: Telemetry write failures
panels.description: Dropped telemetry batches. Above zero, the usage limits are counting low.

panels.title: Rollup age
panels.description: Age of the Postgres-backed gauges. Climbing means the rollup query is failing and the usage/cost numbers above are stale.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: What is deployed.

targets.expr: 100 * (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{env=~"$env", host=~"$host", fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{env=~"$env", host=~"$host", fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"})

description: NetBird AI Assistant. Ordered most-useful first: product health and cost at the top, transport and host plumbing at the bottom.
